summary.headline: Susan Electricals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and PAT turned positive at ₹6.39 Cr, with blended operating margin ~11.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and operating profit rose 980% YoY to ₹11.04 Cr, with PAT of ₹6.39 Cr versus a ₹0.42 Cr loss a year earlier. Management attributed the improvement to higher scale, better product mix and higher EBITDA per unit. Management is shifting the mix toward HT/MVCC and LT cables and is adding 4,500 Km p.a. of capacity (+60%) with commercial operations targeted from Feb 2027. Management declined to give a FY27 revenue number, and several answers on margins and product mix were inconsistent between the prepared remarks and the Q&A.

segments.name: LT cables and conductors
segments.commentary: Management cited ~6.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. Company said winding wires and LT/conductors typically earn 10-15% per unit.

segments.name: HT cables
segments.commentary: Management cited ~7% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. HT/MVCC currently make up ~5-10% of revenue (another answer said 10-15%).

segments.name: Winding wires
segments.commentary: Management cited ~24.39% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27, the highest of the three segments cited.

segments.name: MVCC cables
segments.commentary: Grouped with HT cables by management; no separate margin disclosed. Management targets HT/MVCC potential of ~20% per-unit margin.

guidance_outlook: HT and MVCC share of revenue targeted to rise from ~5-10% toward ~15% by year-end, with 'higher thereafter'. A later answer said ~50% by year-end; this is inconsistent and needs verification.
Expected FY27 revenue mix of roughly 30-35% each across HT/MVCC, LT/conductors and winding wires.
Management expects blended operating margin to be maintained or improved with mix shift and operating leverage.
No absolute FY27 revenue guidance; management said growth momentum will continue and pointed to the last 2-3 years' trajectory.
Capacity expansion on track for commercial operations from Feb 2027, taking capacity from 7,500 Km p.a. to 12,000 Km p.a.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of approximately ₹15-20 Cr, mainly machinery and factory expansion.
Capacity adds 4,500 Km p.a., taking total from 7,500 Km to 12,000 Km p.a. (+60%); commercial operations from Feb 2027.
Management referenced a 'peak capex reference potential' of ~₹700-800 Cr in revenue, which is not clearly defined in the call.
Longer-term plan of aggressive capacity build-out to reach much larger scale in 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹142.39 Cr as of 30 June 2026, with an active pipeline of ₹150 Cr and total visibility of ₹292 Cr.
Order-book mix: ~30% HT/MVCC, ~35% LT cables and conductors, ~35% winding wires; ~50:50 government/DISCOMs vs private/EPC.
Orders are primarily tender-based (central/state utilities and EPC contractors such as Monte Carlo and RVNL); supply starts ~45 days to 2 months after order.
Bidding ₹800-1,200 Cr of tenders with expected conversion of ~15-20%; several pipeline items are L1/L2 awaiting LOI.
Exploring railways and defence; working on empanelment with power sector companies.
Raw material (aluminium rod) price volatility is handled through 'appropriate pricing mechanisms', with no specifics given.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise EBITDA margins for LT cables, HT cables and winding wires?
qa_highlights.answer: LT cables and conductors ~6.5%, HT cables ~7%, winding wires ~24.39% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why are HT cable margins lower and what is the potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current margins reflect early-stage revenue and that operating leverage will help as volumes scale. HT and MVCC have potential of ~20% net margin at product level, depending on scale and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹15-20 Cr, mainly machinery and expansion, with factory expansion commissioning in February.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No absolute number. Management said growth momentum should continue on power-sector demand and pointed to the last 2-3 years' trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall EBITDA margin and product-level clarity?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall company EBITDA margin was ~12% in Q1 FY27. Management said product-level margins vary by mix and scale, and a participant's request for more detailed product margin disclosure was acknowledged.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium rod price swings managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are monitored and handled through pricing mechanisms and operational measures, with no quantification.

qa_highlights.question: Is additional long-term debt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific plan. Management said it would evaluate funding needs based on growth and expansion.

risks_watch: Internal inconsistency: HT/MVCC share of revenue is stated as 5-10%, 10-15%, and a target of ~15% vs ~50% by year-end. Confirm the true mix and the year-end target.

Segment margins disclosed (6.5%, 7%, 24.39%) do not reconcile cleanly with ~11.9% blended margin and the claimed 10-15% per-unit potential for LT/winding wires. Request a clear product-level breakdown.
Q1 revenue growth of 279% likely reflects a low base; the ₹142 Cr order book is to be executed in ~3 months, so Q2 run-rate is key.
Capacity ramp from Feb 2027 and whether demand can absorb 60% more capacity.
Raw material (aluminium) pass-through and margin defence during price volatility.
Funding plan for expansion is open; watch for debt or equity raise versus ₹15-20 Cr capex.
The ₹700-800 Cr 'peak capex reference potential in revenue' is ambiguous and should be clarified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the power-sector outlook, but evasive on FY27 revenue numbers, debt funding and product-level margin detail. Several answers were vague or inconsistent, which suggests the transcript may be unreliable on specific figures.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong start to FY27, supported by robust execution, improving product mix and better EBITDA per unit across our product portfolio.
We would not like to provide an absolute revenue number at this stage.
At present, we are focusing on strengthening our operations and expanding our manufacturing capabilities.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of ₹0.42 Cr in Q1 FY26
